subject: BrightLeaf hybrid gateway: route-sync mismatch causing intermittent TCP resets and MTU anomalies
messages:
From: Sam Brooks <sam@brightleaf.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightLeaf Network Ops <netops@brightleaf.io>
Date: 2026-10-16 11:15 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 502s/connection resets for private deployment (BrightLeaf)

Hi Evelyn / Redwood team,

We've been seeing intermittent failures for our on-prem -> Redwood private deployment over your hybrid gateway since Friday. Symptoms: a subset of requests from our users return 502s or time out, and we see TCP retransmits / RSTs in the return path. It looks like only traffic that traverses our edge firewall policy group GW-OUTBOUND-1 hits the issue.

We captured a short tcpdump during a failed flow (attached) — you can see repeated SYN retransmits from the client, then a SYN from the Redwood node that never completes, and finally a reset. Traceroutes from our edge show asymmetric return paths through a backup route.

What we've tried so far:
- Confirmed our BGP sessions to the colo are up
- Cleared conntrack on the on-prem firewall (temporary, no change)
- Confirmed security groups on the Redwood side appear permissive for the flows

Attaching: brightleaf_tcpdump_snippet.pcap, and a config export of the gateway policy.

Can you help triage? We suspect either a route-programming mismatch at the hybrid gateway or an MTU/fragmentation problem on the GRE/VXLAN path.

Thanks,
Sam Brooks
Network Ops
BrightLeaf
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Brooks <sam@brightleaf.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-16 12:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s/connection resets for private deployment (BrightLeaf)

Hi Sam — thanks for the quick report and the pcap. I've looped in our private-deploy and network reliability leads. We'll treat this as an escalation given the user impact.

Immediate asks:
1) Can you provide a BGP RIB snapshot from the on-prem side and the colo-facing router (one for each side) + the output of `show ip route` for the prefixes to the Redwood private subnet?
2) Please also attach the firewall conntrack counters (`conntrack -L | wc -l`) and an iptables/nft rules export if possible.
3) Which of your edge devices are performing NAT for the client flows (policy name)? Confirm whether return-path policy-based routing exists.

From our side we'll:
- Check hybrid gateway route programming and recent route updates for the tenant
- Verify NAT translation consistency and conntrack entries on the Redwood edge
- Look for MTU mismatches on the tunnel endpoints and any recent kernel changes that could affect fragmentation/MSS.

Can we get the BGP dump and policy export in the next hour? If needed we'll open an immediate call.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Sam Brooks <sam@brightleaf.io>
Date: 2026-10-16 12:28 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s/connection resets for private deployment (BrightLeaf)

Looping in commands and quick checks we want from BrightLeaf before more intrusive steps:
- BGP RIB: `show ip bgp neighbors <colo-peer> received-routes` and `show ip bgp summary`
- Kernel: `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward; sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing`
- Tunnel MTU: `ip link show dev <vxlan0|gre0>` on both ends (physical MTU and inner MTU)
- Conntrack: `conntrack -S` and `conntrack -L | grep <client-ip>` around failed flow timestamps

From our telemetry:
- We see a small but consistent increase in TCP retransmits from the tenant's IP block around the times you reported.
- Route changes: a flapping BGP advertisement at 03:40 UTC appears correlated to many of the failure windows.

If BrightLeaf can provide the bgp_rib_snapshot.txt and the firewall policy export we can diff the advertised next-hops and spot any asymmetry. Also please include your NAT translation table snapshot if possible.

If routing asymmetry is confirmed, temporary mitigations we can coordinate:
- Pinning flows to the primary egress path at the hybrid gateway (sticky routing)
- Applying MSS clamp on the tunnel endpoints (MTU workaround)
- Short maintenance window to roll back the problematic firewall policy if that proves to be the cause.

-Rishi
Senior Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: BrightLeaf Network Ops <netops@brightleaf.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-17 08:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s/connection resets for private deployment (BrightLeaf)

Thanks — attached are the files you requested: bgp_rib_snapshot.txt and fw_policy_export.json. Exported conntrack size: 1,382,420 (we rotated but the counts are stable).

Notes from our side after digging:
- The firewall policy GW-OUTBOUND-1 has a NAT rule that rewrites source IPs but also triggers a return-path policy for some /24s (policy-based routing bound to the NAT rule).
- Your tcpdump (attached previously) matches our local capture: SYNs from client -> SYN from Redwood -> client retransmit -> finally our firewall emits a RST when it times out waiting for a matching connection entry (we see unmatched responses hit a different VRF).
- BGP RIB: we can see the primary path to Redwood's tenant prefix via colo-router-A. However around 03:40 UTC the backup path on colo-router-B becomes preferred for a portion of the prefix due to an iBGP reweight we recently applied as a test. That lines up with your flapping note.

We suspect two simultaneous issues: (1) route convergence caused some flows to land on a path that bypasses the NAT translation state (asymmetric path) and (2) an MTU mismatch on the VXLAN tunnel at the colo caused fragmentation which made the firewall drop fragments because policy evaluation expects full packets.

If you confirm we can do a quick maintenance window tonight to:
- Revert the test iBGP weight change on colo-router-B (prevent the asymmetry)
- Apply an MSS clamp on the VXLAN endpoints (1500 -> 1400) to avoid fragmentation
- Monitor conntrack/translation hits during the window.

Attached: bgp_rib_snapshot.txt, fw_policy_export.json

—BrightLeaf NetOps
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, BrightLeaf Network Ops <netops@brightleaf.io>
Date: 2026-10-17 09:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s/connection resets for private deployment (BrightLeaf)

Thanks for the dumps — good find. Proposed short-term runbook (non-disruptive first):
1) Enable packet capture on the hybrid gateway for the tenant with `tcpdump -s 1500 -w /tmp/bleaf-rtc.pcap host <client-ip> or net <tenant-net>` and tail for SYN,SYN-ACK pairs and retransmits.
2) Enable MSS clamping on both tunnel endpoints: `ip link set dev vxlan0 mtu 1400` and `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` (this avoids in-flight fragmentation).
3) Coordinate with BrightLeaf to revert the temporary iBGP weight on colo-router-B during an agreed 15-minute window.
4) If conntrack misses continue, add a short-lived SNAT policy on the Redwood edge to force symmetric translation for the tenant (controlled rollback possible).

I can lead step 2 and 4 from our side if BrightLeaf schedules the iBGP revert. Proposed window: 2026-10-17 23:30 - 23:45 PDT. Please confirm.

-Dev
Software Engineer, Private Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: BrightLeaf Network Ops <netops@brightleaf.io>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18 09:37 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s/connection resets for private deployment (BrightLeaf)

Quick post-window summary:
- BrightLeaf reverted the iBGP weight on colo-router-B during the 23:30 PDT window. We applied MSS clamp on both tunnel endpoints and observed immediate reduction in fragmentation and retransmits.
- We temporarily enabled a targeted SNAT on the Redwood edge for the affected tenant IP block which eliminated asymmetric conntrack misses.
- Monitoring since 00:15 PDT shows no new 502s and normal TCP RTT/retransmit levels.

Root cause (preliminary): a combination of (A) test iBGP weight change on BrightLeaf's colo-router-B that caused transient path asymmetry, and (B) VXLAN MTU settings that allowed fragments to be produced and dropped by the firewall policy evaluation. The firewall's policy-based return-path handling amplified the impact because replies were arriving on a different VRF without a matching translation entry.

Next steps (owners):
- BrightLeaf: revert the experimental BGP test from colo-router configs permanently and confirm scheduled maintenance for config hygiene (owner: Sam Brooks).
- Redwood (Rishi/Dev): roll out a tenant-scoped persistent MSS clamp to the hybrid gateway template and add a health-check that flags large fragment counts (owner: Rishi).
- Joint: schedule a 1-hour postmortem next week to formalize mitigations and update the runbook (create JIRA RI-2401).

Thanks everyone for the quick coordination. I'll draft a short P0 incident note and share it in the IR channel for follow-up.

—Evelyn
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
